Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the time permitted for the installation of covered safety treatments on any portion of a street adjacent to a school

Attachments.Name: Minutes of the Stated Meeting - January 29, 2026
Proposed Int. No. 202-A Fiscal Impact Statement - City Council

Summary: This bill would require that where a Department of Transportation (DOT) traffic study determines it is appropriate to install a covered safety treatment on any portion of a street adjacent to a school, DOT must complete such installation within 120 days, or 180 days in the case of a traffic control signal, subject to certain exceptions. DOT would also be required to submit a report every two years regarding the installations completed.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the time permitted for the installation of covered safety treatments on any portion of a street adjacent to a school

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subdivision a of section 19-188.2 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding new definitions of “covered safety treatment,” “major transportation project,” “school loading zone,” and “speed reducer” in alphabetical order to read as follows:
Covered safety treatment. The term “covered safety treatment” means a stop sign, speed reducer, traffic control signal, or school loading zone. 
Major transportation project. The term “major transportation project” has the same meaning as set forth in subdivision a of section 19-101.2.
School loading zone. The term “school loading zone” means any area on a street immediately adjacent to a school where the standing or parking of a vehicle is restricted or limited during specified hours on school days.
Speed reducer. The term “speed reducer” has the same meaning as set forth in subdivision a of section 19-185.1.
§ 2. Section 19-188.2 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding new subdivisions d and e to read as follows:
d. Where a traffic study conducted by the department determines it is appropriate to install a covered safety treatment on any portion of a street adjacent to a school, the department shall use reasonable efforts to complete such installation within 120 days, provided that the department shall have 180 days if such covered safety treatment is a traffic control signal. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the department shall not be required to complete any such installation within the time period required by this subdivision if such installation is part of a major transportation project, or where the department determines that completing such installation would be impracticable, or that in its professional engineering judgment such installation would endanger public safety. 
e. No later than December 31, 2028, and no later than December 31 every 2 years thereafter, the department shall post on the department’s website, and submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor, a report regarding the installations completed by the department pursuant to subdivision d of this section during the 2 year period immediately preceding the due date of such report. 
§ 3. This local law takes effect immediately.
